key_insight: In laser–TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, laser power, travel speed, and welding current influence molten-pool flow, weld geometry, and arc stability.
engineering_relevance: These parameter–response relationships can guide welding-process optimization for low-expansion Invar tooling used in aerospace composite manufacturing.
method: Parameter studies: 5–6 kW laser power, 0.5–0.8 m/min speed, and 150–170 A current.
evidence_signal: Within the studied ranges, higher power increased penetration and keyhole size, higher speed reduced penetration and weld width, and higher current widened the weld and stabilized the arc.
watch_item: The abstract provides parameter trends but no quantitative validation errors or final weld-property measurements, limiting assessment of predictive accuracy and joint performance.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
